before: \abstract{Retrieval and structural checks can make a natural-language optimization output appear usable without establishing complete numerical grounding. We study this diagnostic gap through three questions: fixed-catalog schema identification, the validity of coverage/type readiness as a numerical check, and the mechanisms behind grounding outcomes. On 331 queries from the NLP4LP natural-language optimization benchmark and 335 schema documents, term frequency--inverse document frequency retrieval and a pretrained dense encoder identify the target schema for 301 and 313 queries. Ratio-aware lexical grounding passes coarse readiness on 265 queries, but only seven satisfy the complete stored-reference scalar-tolerance criterion: 2.64\% of the readiness-passing population. A mutually exclusive residual partition separates retrieval, coverage, type and numerical failures. Six grounding procedures under fixed retrieval yield between seven and 46 complete successes, while changing candidates, scoring, abstention and decoding together. A separate 49-query frozen-score assignment study improves exact slot counts without increasing the five whole-instance tolerance successes, delimiting what can be attributed to search. The methodological contribution is joint reporting of retrieval, readiness and complete scalar agreement with explicit assistance, denominators and evidence boundaries. Reference-derived inventories and benchmark exposure restrict these findings to assisted grounding. Supplementary relationship judgments and author contrasts assisted by artificial intelligence delimit semantic interpretation without establishing accuracy. A versioned public release supports saved-record reanalysis; missing historical predictions and restricted originals prevent full experimental reproduction.}
